lines.say: In 1945, a farmer in Fruita, Colorado, tried to prepare a chicken for dinner.
shots: a red barn farm in Colorado with mountains behind, autumn
a farmer in overalls holding an axe next to a tree stump, a cheerful rooster nearby, cartoon

lines.say: But the axe missed the brain stem and one ear, and the chicken got up and kept walking.
shots: {hero} walking happily across the farmyard, the farmer dropping his axe in shock
{hero} pecking at the ground like normal, other hens staring

lines.say: The farmer kept him alive by feeding him with an eye dropper. They called him Mike.
shots: the farmer feeding {hero} with a glass eye dropper at a kitchen table, lamp light
a wooden sign that reads nothing, hanging on a chicken coop, sunny

lines.say: Mike became famous. He toured America, and people paid twenty five cents to see him.
shots: {hero} on a small stage under a circus tent with spotlights, crowd cheering
a long line of 1940s people with hats queuing outside a colourful sideshow booth

lines.say: Scientists at the University of Utah even studied him, to understand how he survived.
shots: scientists in white coats examining {hero} on a lab table with old microscopes
{hero} posing for a photographer with an old flash camera

lines.say: Fruita still throws him a party every year, because believe it or not,
shots: {hero} standing on a hill at sunset like a hero
a small golden statue of a headless rooster in a town square

description:
True story: Mike the headless chicken lived 18 months without a head in 1940s Colorado.

What would you have named him? Tell us in the comments.

In 1945, a Colorado farmer's chicken survived losing its head and lived about 18 more months. Mike the Headless Chicken toured the US and still has a festival in Fruita. A true story.

Sources: Fruita, Colorado (Mike the Headless Chicken Festival); Wikipedia: Mike the Headless Chicken.
